node.label: Paul Kennedy
node.description: A historian of international power, strategy and political economy. The Rise and Fall of the Great Powers (1987) argues that great powers decline relative to others when their strategic commitments outrun their economic base; readers summarized this as ‘imperial overstretch’, and in the late 1980s it was read as a warning to the United States. Michael Cox notes that the idea was not wholly new, and Kennedy himself traced one stimulus to Mahan’s use of an earlier reflection on Spain’s dispersed empire. In the same roundtable Varsha Venkatasubramanian criticized the book’s neglect of non-state actors and of politics’ effects on economic development; Kennedy accepted her point about India and conceded that the book may contain too much economic determinism. His earlier books studied British naval mastery and the Anglo-German antagonism before 1914.
